observation_summary: The StringUtils.replaceEach method throws a NullPointerException when an element in the replacementList array is null, as it attempts to call .length() on a null reference.
hypothesis: The method lacks a null check for elements within the searchList and replacementList arrays before accessing their length, causing an NPE when a null value is encountered.
prediction: Adding a conditional check (if (searchList[i] == null || replacementList[i] == null) continue;) inside the loop that calculates the buffer size will prevent the NPE and correctly ignore null entries.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff explicitly adds a null check for both searchList[i] and replacementList[i] before the .length() call, which directly addresses the root cause of the NullPointerException.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic missing guard/validation check. The code attempts to perform an operation (calling .length()) on potentially null array elements without verifying their existence first. Adding this check is the standard way to handle such validation errors in Java, fitting the 'Checking' ODC type perfectly.
evidence_used: Stack trace shows NullPointerException at StringUtils.java:3676
Code snippet at line 3676 calls replacementList[i].length()
Fix diff adds a null check for searchList[i] and replacementList[i] before the length calculation

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is inside a method, the root cause is not an incorrect algorithm or computation, but rather the absence of a necessary guard condition to handle invalid input data.
